info.name: MKirell Portfolio MS
info.description:
# MKirell Portfolio MS

Complete API surface for `mkirell-portfolio-ms` — the portfolio data service behind **mkirell-portfolio-mf** (public reads) and **mkirell-console-mf** (authenticated CRUD).

---

## Setup

1. Import this collection **and** `MKirell Portfolio MS - Development.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the **MKirell Portfolio MS — Development** environment (top-right).
3. Start the service: `cd mkirell-portfolio-ms && npm run dev`.
4. Seed it if you have not: `npm run seed:fresh`.

Start Keycloak too: `cd infra/keycloak && docker compose up -d`.

Folders `00` and `01` work immediately — those endpoints are public.

---

## Signing in

Tokens come from **Keycloak** now, not from the service — see `infra/keycloak`. Postman fetches its own
with the password grant, so there is no browser round-trip and nothing to copy out of DevTools.

Enable it once in the realm (deliberately not in the committed realm file — direct access grants are a
testing affordance, not something a production realm should offer):

1. Admin console → realm `mkirell` → **Clients → Create client**: id `mkirell-postman`, public client,
   **Direct access grants** on, standard flow off.
2. **Users → Add user** with a password, then **Role mapping** → assign `mkirell-portfolio-ms admin`.
3. Fill in `keycloakUser` and `keycloakPassword` in the environment.
4. Run **02 · Auth → Get access token from Keycloak** once.

After that the collection keeps itself signed in: a collection-level pre-request script re-requests the
token whenever it is missing or within a minute of expiring.

> **Why the service never sees a password:** it only ever receives a bearer token, verifies the realm
> signature against the published JWKS, and reads the `admin` client role out of the token's
> `resource_access`. There is no user table here to authenticate against.

---

## Running the whole thing

The collection is safe to run end-to-end in the Collection Runner:

- Each entity folder creates a record, exercises it, and **deletes it** — no residue.
- Locale and UI-string writes target a throwaway `{{sandboxLang}}` (`xx`) language, so your real English and French copy is never touched.
- `PUT /admin/person` sends a faithful copy of the seeded profile, so it is idempotent.

Folder **15 · Security** deliberately sends no token and expects failures. It is included in a full run and should pass — every request there asserts the *rejection*.

---

## Request naming

Every request follows one shape:

```text
<Action> <resource>                    happy path
<Action> <resource> — <code> <reason>  expected failure
```

So `Create experience` is the success case and `Create experience — 400 unknown property` is the matching rejection. The status code sits in the name, so a folder reads as a specification without opening anything.

Entity folders hold only the CRUD lifecycle plus the one validation case specific to that entity. The rules every entity shares — unknown properties, translation-map shape, reorder integrity — live once in **06 · Admin — Experiences**, since they come from `BaseCrudService` and the global `ValidationPipe` rather than from any single resource.

## Variables

| Variable | Where | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | environment | Service origin, e.g. `http://localhost:3000` |
| `apiPrefix` | environment | Path prefix, `api/v1` |
| `accessToken` | environment | Short-lived bearer token, set by the scripts |
| `keycloakUrl` | environment | Realm authority, e.g. `http://localhost:8080` |
| `keycloakRealm` | environment | Realm name, `mkirell` |
| `keycloakClientId` | environment | Public client used for the password grant, `mkirell-postman` |
| `keycloakUser` / `keycloakPassword` | environment | Realm credentials Postman signs in with |
| `accessTokenExpiry` | environment | Epoch ms, drives the pre-emptive token request |
| `lang` | collection | Language used by read requests |
| `sandboxLang` | collection | Throwaway language for destructive write tests |
| `*Id` | collection | Captured from each create, consumed by update/delete |

Set `skipAuthRefresh` to `true` on a request to opt out of the auto-refresh.

item.name: 02 · Auth
item.description:
Authentication is **delegated to Keycloak**. This service issues no tokens; it only verifies them.
There is no `/auth/google`, no `/auth/refresh` and no `/auth/logout` here any more — those are the
realm's endpoints now.

### Signing in

Postman fetches its own token with the password grant, so no browser round-trip is needed. Enable it
once in the realm — it is deliberately absent from the committed realm file, because direct access
grants are a testing affordance rather than something a production realm should offer:

1. Keycloak admin console → realm `mkirell` → **Clients → Create client**: client id `mkirell-postman`,
   public client, **Direct access grants** enabled, standard flow off.
2. **Users → Add user** with a password, then **Role mapping → Assign role** →
   filter by clients → `mkirell-portfolio-ms admin`.
3. Set `keycloakUser` and `keycloakPassword` in the Postman environment.

Run **Get access token from Keycloak** once to confirm; after that the collection-level pre-request
script keeps the token fresh on its own.
